spec.name: type
spec.instructions: What type of message is the MESSAGE?

spec.name: type
spec.instructions: Give the MESSAGE exactly one type; the previous message is context only and is never the one classified.

choices.instructions: The sender places, changes, confirms or cancels a purchase, booking or reservation, or gives the details needed to complete one.
The sender asks for information and is not unhappy about anything, including the status of an order when nothing has gone wrong yet.
The sender says something went wrong or is unsatisfactory, raised for the first time, with no demand beyond a normal fix.
The sender pushes an unresolved problem further: asks for a manager or a human, says it was raised before without result, sets an ultimatum or threatens consequences.
None of the above: greetings, thanks, small talk, reactions, unrelated topics, or messages too fragmentary to place.

spec.name: type
spec.instructions: A message may fit several types; the first that applies in this order wins: escalation, complaint, order, question, other. The content decides, not the form, so a question about something that went wrong is a complaint. Classify the MESSAGE; the previous message is context only.

choices.instructions: The sender commits to a purchase, booking or change, or cancels with nothing wrong.
A plain request for information about the business, or one on which a purchase depends.
Dissatisfaction raised once, in any tone, even when worded as a question or paired with a cancel or return request.
Only with a signal: a repeat of an unresolved problem, including as shown by the previous message, a demand for a human or manager, an ultimatum or a threat.
Nothing above applies, including a question unrelated to the business.

spec.name: type
spec.instructions: Decide first whether anything went wrong. If nothing did, the message is an order, a question or other. If something did, it is a complaint on first mention, and an escalation only when the sender pushes it beyond ordinary handling: a human or manager is demanded, the problem was already raised, there is an ultimatum or a threat to cancel, dispute or review. Angry tone alone does not make an escalation. Classify the MESSAGE; the previous message is context only.

choices.instructions: Nothing went wrong and the sender is buying, booking, changing or cancelling.
Nothing went wrong and the sender wants information about the business.
Something went wrong and it is a first, ordinary report.
Something went wrong and the sender pushes it beyond ordinary handling.
Nothing went wrong and nothing is being asked or bought.

spec.name: type
spec.instructions: Read the MESSAGE with the previous message, which only explains what it refers to. A short reply such as yes, that one or the 14th works is an order when the previous message asked the sender to choose or confirm something for a purchase or booking, and other after anything else. Thanks with a further request is judged by the request. A previous message showing the problem was already raised counts as a repeat. A question unrelated to the business is other.

choices.instructions: Chooses or confirms something for a purchase or booking, or asks for a change or return with nothing wrong.
Asks the business for information about its products, prices, hours, delivery, or order status.
Reports a first problem with a product, delivery, charge or service.
Repeats a problem already raised, or demands a human or manager, or sets an ultimatum.
A reply that fits no purchase or problem, thanks, small talk, or an unrelated topic.
